draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Dandeli! This small Western Ghats town sits on the River Kali, and its class 3 rapids make it one of the best places around for white water rafting.
draft.hungryLine: Grab a kachori or samosa, they're super famous here, and wash it down with a kokum sherbet or a masala soda.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Head out to the ancient Kavala Caves, about 25 km away, or the Kulgi Nature Camp with its little museum and nature centre.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take a coracle ride on the Kali and keep your eyes open for crocodiles and hornbills.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The museum at Kulgi Nature Camp has the stuffed remains of a 13-ft king cobra that was caught in this area.

legends.title: Shiva's forest home
legends.body: Locals revere the Kavala caves as the abode of Lord Shiva. Getting there means climbing thousands of steps through thick forest, which feels like part of the pilgrimage.

tips.title: Set aside half a day for rafting.
tips.body: The Kali rafting route runs around 9 to 14 km over class III rapids and takes about 2 to 3 hours, sometimes more.

tips.title: Sort out Kulgi in advance.
tips.body: Stays at Kulgi Nature Camp are booked through the Forest Conservator's office ahead of time, and meals are charged separately.

story.title: Caves in the forest
story.body: Deep in the forest about 25 km from town are the ancient Kavala caves. People have long revered them as the home of Lord Shiva.

story.title: An industry town grows
story.body: Industries came up in Dandeli, and people moved here from across India to work in them. That's why the town has such a mixed crowd.

story.title: Tigers and rapids
story.body: Dandeli is known for its wildlife sanctuary and is proud of being one of the tiger projects. It's also a gateway to the Kali Tiger Reserve and a favourite for rafting and kayaking on the Kali.
